responsibility: This module implements GCC’s link-time optimization subsystem: the infrastructure that writes intermediate language and interprocedural analysis state into object-file sections, reads it back during link-time compilation, and orchestrates whole-program and LTRANS execution. Its core streamer and section files define the LTO bytecode format, section naming, shared reader/writer state, low-level section I/O, compression, and the serialization/deserialization of GIMPLE, trees, declarations, locations, machine modes, and other metadata. The LTO cgraph logic handles streaming of the interprocedural symbol table, callgraph, varpool, references, and optimization summaries across partitions for WPA and LTRANS, while the options code preserves the effective compilation switches that must be replayed later. At the driver layer, lto-wrapper controls option merging, WPA/LTRANS job execution, temporary files, and parallel job handling, and the LTRANS cache support manages reuse of cached partition inputs and outputs across runs. Overall, this module is the boundary between GCC’s in-memory middle-end/IPA representation and the persisted, link-time whole-program optimization pipeline.
